content.comment_body: I recently acquired several second-hand [product_name] modules and connected them, intending to program them. However, when attempting to upload a program, I am prompted for a password I do not possess. Is there a way to reset the module to restore functionality?
Hello, You may want to look into methods for overwriting a password-protected program on [product_name]. For further guidance, refer to [url]. Hope this assists you.

Thank you for your quick reply. Since I have the Pure version of [product_name] with [article_no] and I am using [product_name] V5.0, the suggested solution did not work for me. Fortunately, the seller provided the correct password via email, and the devices are now functioning properly, so the issue is resolved.
I am experiencing the same issue.

Hi, On older [product_name] modules, entering an incorrect password three times will delete the existing password. Please refer to the corresponding [product_name] manual for your specific version. This process was changed in later versions, such as [product_name] [article_no]. Hope this clarifies things.
The comment by [user_name] dates back to 2009/02/03. I believe the answer is no longer relevant for their situation.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter difficulties programming second-hand [product_name] modules due to password protection, which prevents access and reuse. Solutions are obtained via communication with previous owners for passwords or consulting official manuals and documentation. Password policies vary depending on the module version, which can complicate resolution.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to reset or bypass password protection on [product_name] modules once legitimate ownership is confirmed, thereby enabling programming and continued use of the equipment.
